newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Equitable Bank IPO gets mixed reviews.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Equitable Bank IPO gets mixed reviews.

text.p: Equitable Banking Corp, set to be one of the hottest initial public offerings in the Philippines just weeks ago, has turned off some brokers after it set its IPO price unexpectedly high, analysts said on Tuesday.

The country's ninth largest bank set its offering price at slightly over 19 times its 1997 projected earnings. The valuation is based on the assumption that all warrantholders will buy their allotted shares within the year.
The IPO was priced at 113.30 pesos ($4.31) per share.
"It's a bit expensive. The valuation is too high," said Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities, adding that he would rather advise investors to buy when the shares are listed.
"I've talked to a lot of people, some have a change of heart as far as subscribing to the issue is concerned," Rolando Pineda, chief operating officer of Tower Securities, said.
The 19 times price/earnings ratio was on a par with industry leaders Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co and Philippine Commercial International Bank, analysts said.

"It's a bit aggressive. At 19 times PER, it's actually at par with the industry leaders. I don't think Equitable is in the league of Metrobank, PCIBank or BPI (Bank of the Philippine Islands)," Jonas Ferrer, research head of Pryce Securities, said.
He added that the upside for Equitable shares would be limited to only 15 to 20 percent above the offering price.
Equitable Bank is the ninth largest capitalised bank in a field of more than 40 domestic commercial banks.
The bank said it expected to double its bottom line this year to 2.011 billion pesos ($76.46 million) due to an increase in loanable funds generated from the IPO.
It posted a 47 percent jump in its net income last year to 1.046 billion pesos from 711.267 million pesos in 1995.
Manuel Goseco, chief economist of Dharmala Securities, said the bank's 100 percent growth projection for this year might not be sustainable in the coming years.
"It's still questionable whether it can maintain its growth momentum beyond 1997," Goseco said, although he said he would recommend a "subscribe" for the offering.
An official for lead underwriter EBC Investments Inc said the 19 times valuation was based on the assumption that all its warrantholders exercised the option to subscribe to the shares.
Equitable Bank issued warrants last year which were sold together with its fixed-rate certificates of deposit.

"It's not being offered at a premium. If you based it on a more realistic assumption where only 50 percent of the warrantholders exercise their option this year, the p/e ratio will be only at 17.4 times," he said.
"When you look at it that way, it's not overpriced," he added.
The warrants are exercisable within 12 months from listing. The shares can be bought at the IPO price within the first nine months, and a 10 percent premium in the following three months.
Equitable Bank is offering 85,412,820 shares to the public, 23,240,000 shares of which are underlying shares of its warrants.
The offering period will start on March 5 and ends on March 19. The tentative listing date is on April 3.
Spencer Yap, an analyst at BPI Securities, was bullish on the issue.
"Equitable is strong in a segment which still gives them wide margin, the middle-income and Chinese markets," he said.
The local industry is expected to consolidate in the coming years due to greater competition in a liberalised environment.
